name: Hoxhaism
summary: Hoxhaism is a Marxist-Leninist current named after Enver Hoxha, leader of Albania's Party of Labour, that defends Stalin's legacy and denounces nearly every other communist current as revisionist, including Khrushchev's USSR, Tito's Yugoslavia, Maoist China and Eurocommunism. It demands revolution led by a vanguard party, the dictatorship of the proletariat, central planning and collectivisation, and in Albania it added state atheism and an extreme self-reliance and defence policy.
scope: The anti-revisionist line of Hoxha from the 1960s to his death in 1985, as set out in Imperialism and the Revolution (1978) and applied in Albania under the Party of Labour, plus the later international Hoxhaist parties. Adherents rarely use the label themselves. Excludes Maoism, Titoism and Khrushchevite revisionism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Socialist Albania provided free state health care as part of the planned socialist economy, and adherents treat it as a basic duty of a proletarian state.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wages are set by the socialist state, not a market; the statement presumes a capitalist labour market, so support is inferred from pro-worker principles.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Hoxha insists capitalism is decaying and its market contradictions cannot be reformed; socialism replaces the market with planning.

public-ownership.rationale: Albania nationalised industry and utilities and, as a Marxist-Leninist state, held socialist state property to be the basis of the economy.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Adherents want the bourgeoisie expropriated, not merely taxed; support for higher taxes is a weak inference from hostility to the rich.

unions-good.rationale: Hoxha criticises a worker aristocracy and opportunist union leaders in capitalist countries, while valuing mass organisations of workers under party leadership; the answer is inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: Private ownership of the means of production is the root of exploitation; Albania abolished it and Hoxha upholds Lenin's critique of finance capital.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Adherents hold that regulation cannot fix monopoly capitalism and want it overthrown, yet would not oppose restraints; genuinely indifferent to reform.

cut-welfare.rationale: Hoxha attacks bourgeois states for serving finance capital against workers; a socialist state guarantees social provision.

worker-ownership.rationale: The goal is socialist property, owned by the state and by cooperatives under the party; this is collective ownership but not syndicalist worker control, hence agree rather than strongly agree.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Albania ran a pervasive security service (the Sigurimi) against internal enemies; adherents defend vigilance against subversion.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; Albania's austere moral campaign against Western decadent culture implies opposition.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed directly; adherents would suppress reactionary propaganda but on class grounds, not under a hate-speech concept.

strong-leader.rationale: Party leadership is collective in theory, yet a cult of personality grew around Hoxha; adherents reject bypassing the party for a strongman.

state-harmful.rationale: Hoxha defends the dictatorship of the proletariat and a strong socialist state, and rejects any notion that the state should simply be dismantled.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed in sources; the socialist state monopolised armed force yet also armed the people in a people's war, so support is weak.

empower-police-military.rationale: Albania built a huge defence effort, a people's war doctrine and a security apparatus, to defend socialism against encirclement.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Prostitution is a product of exploitation to be abolished; Albania promoted puritanical morality and women's labour in production.

decide-locally.rationale: Democratic centralism under a single party directed policy nationally, and Albania was highly centralised.

rehabilitation.rationale: Albanian practice combined labour camps with re-education, and enemies of the state were harshly punished; adherents are split between the two aims.

traditional-family.rationale: The regime attacked patriarchal customs and promoted women's emancipation, yet also encouraged large families with Heroine Mother awards.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed by Hoxha; the Albanian regime criminalised homosexuality and rejected Western cultural trends, so opposition is inferred.

abortion-legal.rationale: Under Hoxha abortion was largely restricted and motherhood rewarded, to raise the birth rate.

more-religion-public.rationale: From 1967 Albania declared itself the first atheist state and demolished or converted all churches and mosques as part of the Cultural and Ideological Revolution.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Hoxha supports national liberation and condemns neo-colonial exploitation; domestic racial policy is not addressed, so inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The regime stressed women's emancipation through work, but no source addresses gender theory itself.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Albania stressed national independence and patriotic culture while banning Western cultural influences; adherents also condemn bourgeois nationalism, so agree but not strongly.

gradual-change.rationale: Hoxha rejects the peaceful parliamentary road as counterrevolutionary and demands the destruction of the bourgeois state by revolution.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; Albania was largely closed to movement either way, and adherents frame the matter by class, not by numbers.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Hoxha condemns the UN-style superpower order and insists on national sovereignty and independent revolutions, opposing supranational authority.

free-trade.rationale: Free trade is the means by which monopolies and finance capital export capital and dominate poorer countries, per Hoxha's account of neo-colonialism.

nation-first.rationale: Hoxha defends national sovereignty and self-reliance yet insists that proletarian internationalism ties each country's interests to the world's peoples.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Hoxha holds imperialist wars are predatory and only people's liberation wars are just; interventions by powers are seen as hegemonic aggression.

open-borders.rationale: Albania sealed its borders and treated leaving as treason; open borders are a distant communist aim at most, not a position in the sources.

limit-growth.rationale: Albania pursued rapid socialist industrialisation and self-sufficiency; the idea of capping growth is alien to the doctrine.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: An anachronistic issue that Hoxha never addressed; adherents would blame capitalism but have no distinct programme.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Albania lacked modern technology and valued it for production, but problems are held to be solved by revolution, not technology.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; Hoxha condemned superpower nuclear arsenals, yet backed industrial self-reliance in energy.

revolution-justified.rationale: Hoxha argues socialism arrives only by revolution and armed struggle, and denounces the peaceful parliamentary road.

experts-over-public.rationale: Party and masses are held to lead; adherents distrust bourgeois specialists, yet value technical expertise under party control.

central-planning.rationale: Albania ran a centrally planned state economy, which Hoxhaists defend against the revisionists' market reforms.

socialized-markets.rationale: Hoxha called Yugoslav self-management market socialism anti-Marxist, a revisionist path back to capitalism.

land-value-tax.rationale: A bourgeois reform of capitalism; Albania abolished private landownership instead via land reform and collectivisation.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Property inheritance is not defended; the socialist state expropriated large holdings, so heavy taxation is an inferred, weak position.

basic-income.rationale: Socialist Albania tied income to labour and required work; an unconditional income runs against 'to each according to work' in socialism.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Albania used a state foreign-trade monopoly and self-reliance to protect its industry from imperialist domination.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The state plan directed all investment in Albania's economy.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Albania collectivised agriculture and nationalised industry; small property is a basis for capitalism to re-emerge.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Communism is the ultimate aim, but socialism retains money and wages for the long transition, so agree rather than strongly.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A socialist state controls all banking; abolishing central banks for a free market is the opposite of its economy.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Hoxha attacks class collaboration and social-democratic corporatism as betraying the proletariat, who should be led by the party.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Party of Labour's leading role was enshrined in Albania's 1976 constitution, and Hoxhaists defend the Marxist-Leninist party's leadership.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Albania abolished the monarchy under Zog in 1944-46 and a Marxist-Leninist rejects hereditary rule.

democracy-best.rationale: Adherents call socialist state power proletarian democracy and dismiss bourgeois parliamentary democracy, so they do not endorse the statement as worded.

direct-votes.rationale: Mass participation was claimed through party-led organisations; referendum-style direct legislation is not a doctrine.

workers-councils.rationale: Power belongs to the proletariat led by its party in a state, not to autonomous councils; Hoxha criticises self-management schemes.

right-to-secede.rationale: Hoxha upholds the Leninist right of nations to self-determination but defends sovereign states; no clear stance on regions.

natural-rulers.rationale: Marxism-Leninism denies innate rulers; rule belongs to the proletariat and its party, and class position explains domination.

political-violence-never.rationale: Hoxha endorses revolutionary armed struggle and the dictatorship of the proletariat.

war-builds-character.rationale: Hoxha condemns imperialist wars as predatory, though he praises just liberation wars; he does not celebrate war itself.

separate-church-state.rationale: Albania enforced separation of religion from state, but went further and banned religion; adherents agree with separation while seeking to eliminate religion.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Albania's state atheism and demolition of churches and mosques reflect the doctrine's rejection of religion in law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Hoxha holds the state to be the instrument of class rule that must be in proletarian hands, not privatised.

military-superiority.rationale: Albania stressed a defensive people's war and self-reliance, not superiority over rivals, though adherents want a strong defence.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Hoxhaists oppose bourgeois nationalism and stress class and internationalism over ethnicity; Albania's ethnic politics are not a doctrinal source.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Hoxha says class struggle between the proletariat and the bourgeoisie is intensifying and drives the epoch of imperialism and proletarian revolution.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Socialism removes class exploitation and Albania cut pay differentials and abolished military ranks, though full equality is the later communist stage.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; Hoxha supports national liberation but gives no view on indigenous land rights.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Hoxha condemns colonial and neo-colonial exploitation; reparations are not discussed so the stance is inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Hoxha rejects groupings along such lines; he organises by class and proletarian internationalism and condemns the non-aligned bloc.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Hoxha attacks bourgeois individualism and finance capital's pursuit of profit, stressing collective and socialist morality.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Albania's 1976 constitution tied rights to duties to the state and society, and the regime emphasised sacrifice for the collective.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: An anachronistic question the sources do not address.

limit-population.rationale: The regime encouraged high birth rates, with Heroine Mother awards.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Albania pursued industrialisation as a goal of socialist construction.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Socialism seeks planned development within existing institutions; Hoxha rejects disruption for its own sake.

human-enhancement.rationale: An anachronistic issue the sources do not address.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; the party leads and the masses take part, so adherents would reject ceding decisions to algorithms.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed; given the security state's controls on information, adherents would oppose it.

restore-past-order.rationale: The ideology looks forward to socialism and communism and condemns restoration of capitalism as a revisionist betrayal.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Hoxhaists stress ideological purity against revisionism, treating deviation from Marxism-Leninism as betrayal whatever its practical results.

direct-action.rationale: Hoxha opposes both parliamentary reformism and putschist or adventurist methods, requiring a party-led, prepared revolution.

means-match-ends.rationale: Hoxha holds the dictatorship of the proletariat and revolutionary violence are the means to socialism, so means need not look like the end.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Contrary to a doctrine of industrial socialist construction and historical materialism.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Albania stressed narrowing the town-country and manual-mental gap in the long term but retained specialised labour; ultimate communist aim only.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution by need is the communist stage; under socialism distribution follows work, so adherents agree as an ultimate aim.

production-for-use.rationale: Hoxha holds capitalism produces for profit and socialist planning for the people's needs.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Hoxha reaffirms Lenin: the contradiction between social production and private appropriation, with finance capital and a bourgeoisie living on surplus value.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Hoxha calls the dictatorship of the proletariat necessary after seizing power and accuses revisionists of abandoning it.

collective-farming.rationale: Albania collectivised agriculture, with resisters imprisoned or exiled, and held this to be the socialist road.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Hoxha argues rivalry among imperialist powers over markets and resources drives local and world wars.

taxation-theft.rationale: A socialist state raises revenue for collective purposes; the idea is a bourgeois individualist one Hoxha opposes.

harm-principle.rationale: Albania's state regulated culture, dress and religion, and punished class enemies, so liberal limits on the state are rejected.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rights are framed by class and duties to society; the constitution restricted liberties for the socialist order.

conscription.rationale: Albania relied on a universal people's army and a people's war doctrine requiring mass military service.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Albania made attempting to flee abroad treason under Article 47 and restricted travel.

state-as-business.rationale: Hoxha condemns the bourgeois state as the servant of monopolies; a socialist state serves the working class, not customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Hoxha argues formal independence or freedom without economic emancipation is hollow, a view consistent with material conditions for freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Hoxha sees finance capital and the oligarchy as the real power over governments, not media or universities.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Marxism-Leninism explains inequality by class and social conditions, rejecting racial hierarchy.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation is through the Party of Labour and mass organisations of a socialist state; corporatist bodies are rejected.

total-state.rationale: The Albanian party-state directed the economy, education and culture in the Cultural and Ideological Revolution, though adherents do not call it a total state.

national-rebirth.rationale: The framing is fascist; Hoxha speaks of proletarian revolution and a decaying capitalism, not national decadence and rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Hoxha condemns imperialist and social-imperialist expansion as predatory.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal vassalage is alien to the doctrine; authority rests on the party and the working class.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is the opposite of socialism; Albania's agrarian reform ended landlord power.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Marxism holds ideas reflect class interests, and the Cultural and Ideological Revolution policed culture accordingly; Hoxhaists also claim Marxism-Leninism is objectively true.

universal-morality.rationale: Morality is class-based in the Marxist view, though adherents claim scientific truth for their own doctrine.

single-common-good.rationale: The party is held to represent the proletariat's single interest, but this is class-based, not a common good for all.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Hoxha condemns the Israeli state in the Arab struggle and attacks Zionism as an imperialist tool.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Albania had worker participation and control campaigns within party-led management, but Hoxha criticised self-management as revisionist; adherents are split.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education is state run and ideologically directed in the socialist state, with private schooling abolished.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: A bourgeois fiscal debate that Hoxha does not address; adherents have no stated view.

economic-freedom.rationale: Hoxha holds that real freedom requires abolishing private capital; economic freedom in the market sense maintains exploitation.

rule-by-example.rationale: Albania relied on law, party discipline and repression alongside the leader cult.

national-self-determination.rationale: Hoxha upholds the Leninist right of peoples to independence and sovereignty from imperialism, but subordinates it to class struggle.

force-without-un.rationale: Hoxha condemns UN-sanctioned superpower politics and aggression by powers equally, and approves only just liberation wars.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Dialectical materialism and state atheism uphold science against religion, though 'only' guide overstates.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; Albania was closed to immigrants and welfare was tied to socialist labour.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Socialism holds 'he who does not work shall not eat'; Albanian rights were tied to labour duties.

class-collaboration.rationale: Hoxha attacks social democrats and revisionists for class collaboration, urging intensified class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The Albanian regime demolished religious buildings, but defended national heritage and rejected Western avant-gardes.

dominated-front.rationale: Hoxha rejects the three worlds theory and non-aligned bloc as preserving the status quo, insisting on revolution led by communist parties.

workers-nation.rationale: Hoxha holds the proletariat's interests are inseparable from those of the world's workers, a proletarian internationalism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The regime pushed women into jobs and public office, though it promoted motherhood.

ban-interest.rationale: Interest as such is not a doctrinal issue in the sources; no clear position.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Marxism-Leninism condemns racial oppression as a tool of imperialism and the bourgeoisie.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Hoxha says the bourgeois state serves the financial oligarchy and suppresses resistance, restating Marx and Lenin.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Albania exploited its own oil, gas and coal for self-sufficiency; the issue is inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory unlike Hoxha's class analysis; he blames finance capital, not an immigration plot.

proportional-representation.rationale: Elections in Albania were party-controlled; bourgeois electoral systems are held to be a facade, so only weak opposition to reform.

national-mission.rationale: Hoxha condemns exporting systems by force and insists revolution 'is not exported'.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The regime campaigned against patriarchal custom and for women's emancipation, framing it by class rather than by gender.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Hoxha describes revisionist leaders as a new bourgeoisie with privileges and Western elites as servants of finance capital.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is rejected by Marxism-Leninism, which treats social conditions as decisive.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The Sigurimi's repression was defended as protecting socialism, and Hoxhaists do not accept accountability for it.

night-watchman-state.rationale: A socialist economy needs a state running the economy; Hoxha rejects the liberal minimal state as bourgeois.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contrary to internationalism and Marxist anti-racism.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Marxists affirm human equality but frame rights by class and deny equal rights to class enemies under the dictatorship of the proletariat.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Hoxha insists revolution is not exported, defends building socialism in Albania alone and rejects the revisionist denial that it can be lasting without it.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Hoxha condemns colonialism and neo-colonialism and the Israeli state; the general statement is an inference.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Albania enforced one law for all and abolished religious courts and clergy authority.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The regime banned all religion rather than regulating conversion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Alien to Albania's secular socialist policy; no religious restrictions on food, and collective farming for meat production.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: State education in Albania was atheist, and religion was banned from 1967.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Hoxha holds that as long as imperialism and social-imperialism threaten, the dictatorship of the proletariat must be strengthened, and Albania built mass defence.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Legitimacy rests on class and party leadership of the proletariat rather than on consent as such, though adherents claim popular support.

trade-surplus.rationale: Albania pursued self-reliance, but a surplus aim is not a stated doctrine.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of minorities is not a stated aim in the sources; inferred opposition from internationalism.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Hoxha endorses revolutionary violence and the dictatorship of the proletariat.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Hoxha sees class struggle, not competition among individuals or peoples, as the engine.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The Albanian state outlawed all parties except the Party of Labour and suppressed counterrevolution, and adherents would ban parties of the bourgeoisie.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Hoxha discusses exploitation and domination by finance capital but not this republican concept.

separated-powers.rationale: Albania had a unified system of power under the party; separation of powers is dismissed as a bourgeois device.

vanguard-party.rationale: Hoxha says the proletariat needs a vanguard Marxist-Leninist party to educate and lead it.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Socialism serves workers and peasants, though framed by class power more than charity.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing was state owned under Albanian socialism and private property accumulation is opposed.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes in capitalist states are supported against the bourgeoisie, yet were not permitted against the socialist state; split.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The Marxist analysis ascribes poverty to exploitation and capitalism, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Hoxhaism holds class, not ethnicity, determines cohesion, and stresses internationalism.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Offices were filled through the party; lotteries have no place in the doctrine.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The dictatorship of the proletariat suppresses counterrevolution without bourgeois legal limits, and Albania did so against internal enemies.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Prices were state-set in Albania's planned economy.

party-controls-media.rationale: All Albanian media were party-state controlled and Western cultural material banned.

party-commands-army.rationale: The Party of Labour directed the army through political commissars, and the Maoist-style people's war doctrine put it under party control.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The Marxist-Leninist model of Paris Commune pay and Albania's egalitarian pay policies point this way, though not stated directly.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Democratic centralism binds members to adopted decisions, and Hoxha insists on a disciplined Marxist-Leninist party.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Hoxha defends national sovereignty and condemns imperialist unions; Eurocommunists and the EU are seen as instruments of capital.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Armed forces answer to the party, not to a president; the formal head of state was ceremonial.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Religion was banned altogether in Albania, so church governance is moot and rejected.

clerical-rule.rationale: Clerical authority is the opposite of state atheism.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Hoxha calls imperialist wars predatory and backs the Leninist line of proletarian opposition, though his focus is on just liberation wars.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The Cultural and Ideological Revolution banned Western material and policed art, though to serve socialism rather than to promote virtue as such.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Hoxha led the party for forty years and no term limits existed; adherents see leadership as party matter.

recall-officials.rationale: Marxist-Leninists endorse recall as in the Paris Commune, although Albanian practice was party controlled.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Albania left the Warsaw Pact in 1968, rejected foreign bases and relied on self-reliance, though it sought common anti-imperialist support.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: State housing was the norm; the aim of family home ownership is not a doctrine.

people-in-arms.rationale: Albania adopted a Maoist-style people's war doctrine with mass bunkers, though it kept a standing army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The aim is narrowing town-country gaps, not romanticising rural life, while peasants were collectivised.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Hoxha raised the Kosovo Albanian question, but no source gives a settled doctrine.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The regime campaigned against intellectual elitism but valued education; split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Hoxha says nations take different paths and respects national sovereignty; ranking cultures is not a doctrine.

death-penalty.rationale: Albania applied the death penalty for treason and attempted escape.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The regime promoted women's emancipation but also a strict moral line; no clear answer.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: State atheism and scientific materialism in schools make creationism unthinkable.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Albania banned Western decadent cultural products as bourgeois corruption.

minority-language-support.rationale: Albania recognised some minorities, but its policy is not a clear doctrinal matter.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The regime banned religion and offered no exemptions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The Cultural and Ideological Revolution enforced conformity, banning Western styles and even beards.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Hoxha denounces neo-colonial exploitation by finance capital, so cancelling debts follows by inference.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Hoxha says formal independence is hollow while neo-colonial dependence and local bourgeois exploitation continue.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Albania adopted constitutions through party-led bodies; Hoxhaists have no stated view on constituent assemblies.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The 1976 constitution restricted liberties for building socialism, and adherents justify this under the dictatorship of the proletariat.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Hoxha condemns capital export and 'aid' as imperialist, though he demands real aid to revolutionary struggles; split.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Albania never sought nuclear weapons and Hoxha condemned superpower arsenals; unclear.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The head of state was chosen through the party-led legislature, and adherents see bourgeois elections as a facade.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The state controls banking under the plan, and an independent central bank is a bourgeois device.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Adherents reject private property rather than conditioning it; agree only weakly in the sense that property is justified by social use.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Hoxha says capitalism was restored after Stalin, calling the USSR social-imperialist with a new Soviet bourgeoisie, though he praises Stalin's era as socialist.

precautionary-principle.rationale: An anachronistic issue the sources do not address.

collective-defense.rationale: Albania left the Warsaw Pact in 1968 over the Czech invasion, rejecting bloc obligations, though it once valued socialist alliance.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Hoxha condemned the 1968 invasion of Czechoslovakia and superpower aggression, so unlawful occupation is condemned.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The state banned and destroyed religious institutions, an extreme form of subordination.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The head of state was a ceremonial figure under the party.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Hoxha called Titoite decentralisation and market socialism anti-Marxist; a region with its own system is not endorsed.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Opposed to monarchy and religion; the leader cult was secular.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Flat income tax is a bourgeois fiscal device; the sources give no direct view, so opposition is inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Materialism holds social being determines consciousness, and the regime sought to remould people through education.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The party stood above the constitution in practice but the doctrine does not say so; split.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The doctrine upholds unified proletarian power, not rule shared among classes.

leader-cult.rationale: Albania under the Party of Labour filled public life with portraits, statues and mass praise of Hoxha and Stalin, though Hoxhaist theory credits the party and masses rather than the nation; support is inferred from that practice and is contested.

equal-parenting.rationale: Hoxhaism never addressed custody after separation; its commitment to equality of women and a state-run family law points neither clearly for nor against a fixed equal-time presumption.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Hoxha held that class struggle continues under socialism and that revisionist leaders restore capitalism, which is his core charge against Khrushchev, Tito and Mao.

land-redistribution.rationale: Hoxha and the Party of Labour carried out the post-1945 land reform, taking land from large owners, before moving to collectivisation.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from proletarian internationalism and support for national liberation: displaced peoples should return.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred: Hoxha backed Albanians in Kosovo within a Yugoslav republic, not changed borders, and opposed nationalism as a bourgeois tool.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Albania banned religion and became a state-atheist country; the doctrine treats religion as an enemy of the people, so punishing apostasy is its opposite.

women-must-cover.rationale: The regime fought the veil and religious practice as backward and oppressive, and opposed religious dress codes.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred: Hoxha attacked imperialist economic blocs and defended national economic independence.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred: Hoxhaism is proletarian internationalism by class, not union by ancestry, and treats nationalism as bourgeois.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninists in the Stalinist tradition rejected national-cultural autonomy in favour of the class struggle and a unitary party.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from proletarian internationalism: struggle together with workers where one lives; Hoxha opposed Zionism.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Hoxha defends Marxist-Leninist historical materialism, with the mode of production as the base of social change.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred: Hoxhaism seeks to abolish capitalism and its markets, not to preserve competition among private firms.

no-bailouts.rationale: Industry is state-owned under central planning, so the statement hardly applies.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Hoxhaism rejects bourgeois democracy but vests power in the party; there is no stated line on majority versus courts.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred: the Party of Labour promoted women in public life as part of socialist construction.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Albania under Hoxha pursued extreme self-reliance and broke with the USSR and China, and Hoxha rejected foreign credit.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred: Hoxha rejected capitalist trade institutions and did not use trade agreements as a lever.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred: the Albanian campaigns of the 1960s and 70s curbed wage differentials and stressed political and moral motivation, against Soviet material incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Inferred: Hoxha stressed the party-led vanguard with the masses, and criticised adventurist armed action as left revisionism.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Party of Labour ended the Albanian monarchy and its beys and agas; Hoxhaism opposes any rank by birth.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Hoxha's Albania stressed national heritage and patriotism alongside proletarian internationalism; inferred from Albanian practice.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Hoxha condemns imperialism and colonial domination and backs national liberation, so rule by a "more advanced" society is rejected.

patriotic-education.rationale: Albania's Party of Labour combined patriotism with socialist education; support is inferred from its self-reliance and national-defence stress.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Hoxhaism frames discrimination as a class and imperialist problem; it has no stated line on admissions preferences, so split or indifferent.

public-money-creation.rationale: Albania's planned economy put banks and credit under the state, and Hoxhaism holds that the socialist state controls the economy.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Hoxha holds that capitalism and imperialism are in deepening crisis that class struggle will bring to revolution.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Hoxha denounces Soviet social-imperialism and great-power spheres of influence as imperialist.

delink-world-market.rationale: Albania pursued extreme self-reliance and rejected dependence on foreign credit, and Hoxha urges peoples to rely on their own forces.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Hoxha holds that workers of all lands, including developed capitalist countries, are exploited and are the revolutionary class.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Hoxhaism wants collective and state control of property and enforced equality, not private owners' discretion.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Hoxhaism rejects bourgeois rights as class instruments in favour of the dictatorship of the proletariat; inferred from that doctrine.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Hoxha backed national liberation and denounced imperialist domination of peoples; voiding imposed colonial borders is inferred from that anti-imperialism.

elective-rulers.rationale: Hoxhaism rejects hereditary rule as feudal and holds that power belongs to the people through elected councils under party leadership.

minority-veto.rationale: Democratic centralism binds minorities to the majority line, and the dictatorship of the proletariat overrides dissenters.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Hoxhaism endorses revolution against bourgeois rulers but not liberal constitutional resistance, and it punished dissent in Albania, so the question fits poorly.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Hoxha treats bourgeois parliaments as a facade of capitalist rule; supreme authority lies in the party-led proletarian state, though the question is about monarchy versus parliament, so this is inferred.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Marxist-Leninist texts do not address animal sentience; no position is documented and none is safely inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Albanian collectivised agriculture used livestock for food as normal practice; support for humane limits is inferred, not documented.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Hoxhaism sees charity from the wealthy as bourgeois paternalism and holds that the exploiting classes must be abolished, not made benevolent.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Hoxhaism demands active, organised participation in class struggle under the party, and condemns withdrawal as desertion.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Hoxha describes bourgeois and revisionist culture and media as tools that dull class consciousness and serve the ruling order.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Hoxha stresses that the bourgeoisie rules through the state, ideology and revisionist agents as well as force; the consent-through-culture framing is inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Hoxha's theory of imperialism holds that the great powers and monopolies plunder the resources and labour of poor countries.

native-born-offices.rationale: Hoxhaism is internationalist in class terms yet Albania ran its own nationalist line; no documented position on native-born office-holding.

party-own-road.rationale: Hoxha holds that each party must lead its own revolution and that revolution is not exported, but he also condemned parties that took other roads as revisionist and demanded one correct Marxist-Leninist line.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Self-reliance was the Albanian line: the 1976 constitution banned foreign credits and investment, and Hoxha broke with the USSR and China over dependence.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Hoxhaism is internationalist in doctrine, while Albania did voice concern for Albanians in Kosovo; no clear position on reclaiming lost territory.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Hoxhaism puts leadership in the proletariat and its party, not in descent groups; the negative answer is inferred from its class basis.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The Albanian communists took power out of the wartime anti-fascist resistance and Hoxhaism keeps anti-fascism central, though it frames a constitution around socialism rather than anti-fascism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Hoxhaism defends Stalin and regards fascism as the open dictatorship of finance capital, so equating it with communism is rejected.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Marxist analysis treats the Civil War as a clash between slave-owning and industrial capital, so slavery was its central cause.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Albania removed monuments of the old order, notably statues and religious buildings; support for preserving condemned figures is rejected by inference from that practice.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Hoxhaism treats inequality as class based and champions women's emancipation; special attention to male disadvantage is not part of it, which is inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Official socialist doctrine frames women's oppression as a legacy of patriarchy and capitalism; symmetry claims are inferred as rejected.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Hoxha rejected imitating foreign models and insisted on Albanian conditions, yet held that socialism is universal; support for distinct forms is inferred and limited.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Hoxhaism insists that the army be a people's army under party command, and in Albania the military held a defensive guardian role subject to the party.

paid-care-work.rationale: Albanian socialism aimed at socialising housework through nurseries and services; wages for household work specifically is inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Hoxha attacked patriarchal custom while promoting the socialist family; the sources give no line on filial duty, so adherents are split.

office-by-exam.rationale: The Party of Labour filled posts by class background and party loyalty rather than competitive exams; inferred from Albanian practice.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The 1976 constitution banned foreign credits and investment, and Hoxha insisted on strict self-reliance, so foreign control of firms is rejected.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Marxist-Leninist family law treats marriage as a civil matter and eases divorce; inferred, not sourced for Albania.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Hoxha speaks of the masses holding officials to account, though the vanguard party remains in command; inferred and contested.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Hoxha rejects capitalist financial institutions and holds that the socialist state provides for the old through the planned economy.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land was collectivised and held by the state and cooperatives, not by individuals as private property, though not on a use-it-or-lose-it basis.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The People's Assembly formally approved budgets but the party set them; the line is unstated and adherents would treat it as formal.

single-official-language.rationale: Albania used Albanian as its common language; the ideology has no stated doctrine on restricting others.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Hoxha's self-reliance and bans on foreign ownership imply land held by the nation, not foreigners.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Hoxha analyses society by class, not by racial outcomes, so disparate-impact tests are inferred to be rejected as bourgeois framing.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Hoxha attacks the bourgeois consumer way of life and stresses austerity and self-reliance; inferred from these.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Hoxha backs national liberation movements and armed struggle against imperialism, including by material aid.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Hoxha condemned the 1968 invasion of Czechoslovakia and Soviet social-imperialism, and withdrew Albania from the Warsaw Pact.

corporate-influence.rationale: Hoxha describes capitalist states as ruled by monopolies and finance capital that dominate politics.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Albania under Hoxha pursued extreme self-reliance and barred foreign credits and bases; inferred that it would limit foreign money in civil society.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Socialist Albania promoted high birth rates; inferred, and the ideology has no stated line on immigration.

residents-only-property.rationale: Land and housing were state-owned and not traded in a market, so the statement's premise does not apply.

job-guarantee.rationale: Socialist planning in Albania made work a right and a duty with state provision of jobs; inferred from planned economy principles.

democratic-peace.rationale: Hoxha holds that bourgeois democracy is a dictatorship of the bourgeoisie and that imperialism, not regime type, causes war.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The proletarian state's laws are binding and to be enforced by the dictatorship of the proletariat; inferred from his view of the state.

non-intervention.rationale: Hoxha condemns superpower interference and social-imperialism and says revolution is not exported, but he supports internationalist aid, so not absolute.

industrial-unions.rationale: Trade unions were treated as transmission belts of the party, and the ideology has no line on industrial versus craft structure.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Hoxhaism denounces imperialist and revisionist plots but not ethnic or religious minority conspiracies; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Albania kept the family as a basic unit and regulated marriage by state law; inferred from regime practice.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Party of Labour ruled a closed, secretive state and gave no right to demand records; inferred from regime practice.

local-production.rationale: Self-reliance meant producing domestically wherever possible; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: Hoxha insists revolution needs a disciplined Marxist-Leninist vanguard party, rejecting spontaneous small groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Hoxha defends national sovereignty and independence against imperialist and revisionist powers, so national authority ranks over foreign bodies.

religious-nation.rationale: Albania under Hoxha declared itself the first atheist state in 1967 and suppressed religion, so religion cannot define the nation.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Hoxha denounced superpower hegemony and social-imperialism and held that states should be sovereign and equal, so tribute to a leading power is rejected.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: A centrally planned economy pools resources across regions under the party's plan; inferred from Albania's planning, as regional retention is not addressed.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Hoxhaist Marxism-Leninism keeps personal property while collectivising land and the means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Hoxhaism seeks the victory of communism and treats it as the goal, rejecting any stance that it should be defeated.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Albania under Hoxha ran health, education and all services directly through the state with no private provision.

religion-illusion.rationale: Albania under Hoxha declared itself an atheist state in 1967, in line with the Marxist view that religion is an illusion that will wither away.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marxism-Leninism treats capitalism as a historically progressive stage before socialism; inferred as Hoxha stresses imperialism as its moribund final stage.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Marxist-Leninist doctrine ties women's emancipation to socialist transformation of the economy; inferred, with Albania's state-led emancipation as an example.

socialized-care.rationale: Marxist-Leninist doctrine looks to socialising domestic work; inferred, as Hoxha's texts used here do not address it.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Albania pursued a unified literary language, but a purge of loanwords is not a documented Hoxhaist position.

treaties-binding.rationale: The ideology has no documented line on treaties with internal nations; a party-led state would revise them as policy required.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Hoxhaism relies on state ownership and central planning, with collectives under the party's plan, not autonomous self-governing communities; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: No documented position; Albania was ethnically homogeneous and the issue is unaddressed.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Hoxha held that socialism built on Marxist-Leninist lines is the only alternative to capitalism and condemned all supposed third ways as revisionism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Proletarian internationalism rejects ethnic or religious claims to land, though Hoxha championed Albanian national interests; inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Hoxhaism is a militantly anti-fascist Stalinist current and has no reason to deny Nazi crimes.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Albania under Hoxha criminalised homosexuality; the sources do not discuss the doctrine's position, so this is inferred from practice.

suppress-opposition.rationale: It demands the dictatorship of the proletariat and denounces opposition as revisionist or bourgeois.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The Albanian state banned religion in 1967 and punished its practice, an extreme form of punishing open practice of religion.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Imperialism and the Revolution condemns imperialism and colonial exploitation.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Hoxhaism backs peoples' national liberation struggles but rejects religious obligation as an organising principle.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Religion is held to be an instrument of reaction, and Hoxhaism rejects rule by religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: It claims mass participation through the party's mass line and workers' control, but within a one-party framework; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: It puts class struggle first and treats other oppressions as subordinate to it, though it promoted women's emancipation.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from its Stalinist social conservatism; not discussed in sources.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from Stalinist social norms and the lack of any doctrine on it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Hoxhaism sees only class struggle and denounces centrist and third-way positions as revisionism.

alienated-labor.rationale: It follows Marxist-Leninist analysis of capitalist exploitation, which includes the alienated nature of wage labour.

islam-incompatible.rationale: It opposed all religions as reactionary but does not frame Islam as culturally incompatible with the West; inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: State atheism and materialism reject any divine source of authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Albania banned religion in public life and Hoxhaism holds religion has no place in state institutions.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred: it favours curbing employer power over workers; the specific question is not discussed.

social-market-economy.rationale: It condemns market-based mixed economies as revisionism restoring capitalism and demands central planning.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Albania under Hoxha fortified the country with bunkers and an armed-people doctrine; the state is defended by arms.

rich-first.rationale: Hoxhaism denounced Deng's China for letting some get rich first as restoring capitalism.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Albania left the Warsaw Pact in 1968 and Hoxha opposed both superpowers' blocs as imperialist.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hoxha ran a party-state that called itself a proletarian dictatorship and rejected hereditary privilege as feudal, in line with Marxism-Leninism.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Hoxhaism wanted state ownership of banks under central planning, not user-owned banks; adherents reject profit banks but also the cooperative alternative; inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Hoxha held up extreme self-reliance and refused foreign credits, and denounced the IMF and foreign capital as imperialist tools.

property-franchise.rationale: Hoxhaism holds that political power belongs to the working people under the dictatorship of the proletariat, so a property or tax bar on voting is the bourgeois opposite.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Hoxhaism does not take up ecofeminist theory, which it would treat as bourgeois idealism, though it backed women's emancipation; inferred.

reification.rationale: The claim restates Marx's commodity fetishism, which Hoxha's orthodox Marxism-Leninism accepts as a critique of capitalism.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Hoxha held that bourgeois freedoms are formal because the capitalists own the press and halls, and that real freedom needs socialist ownership.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Party of Labour ruled by party directive and a security state, not by independent judges applying standing laws.

racial-franchise.rationale: Hoxhaism is internationalist and rejects racism as a bourgeois tool, and the Albanian constitution gave rights by class, not by ethnic group.

online-participation.rationale: The ideology predates the internet and held that deliberation happens through the party, so adherents would not push online participation; inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: The Party of Labour ran a closed security state and adherents would accept openness only inside the party; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Albania under Hoxha banned religion outright, and marriage between believers was not a concern of the state; adherents would reject religion-based marriage law.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Hoxhaism rejects national and religious hatred as bourgeois division of the working class and denounces such discrimination.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Hoxhaism puts rule in a vanguard party under democratic centralism, so lot-chosen assemblies are inferred as incompatible with it.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Hoxha banned religion in 1967 as backward and sought its elimination rather than its modernisation; the rejection of reform is inferred from that.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Hoxhaism holds that private accumulation of capital produces a ruling bourgeoisie that dominates the state, and that only socialist ownership ends it.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred: Albania under Hoxha criminalised homosexuality and promoted a rigid, puritan moral order, and nothing in the doctrine would favour open service.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Hoxha's Albania closed all places of worship in 1967 and declared itself the world's first atheist state, with atheist propaganda in schools.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Hoxhaism demands the dictatorship of the proletariat, and Hoxha's Albania ran the Sigurimi secret police and a network of prison camps to defend it.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Hoxhaism rejects power-sharing between social groups in favour of the single vanguard party's leadership, and treats national questions through proletarian internationalism.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Hoxhaism treats charity as bourgeois and holds that the socialist state must guarantee welfare through planning.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred: Hoxha ruled the party for four decades and the party's leadership was not subject to term limits, though rotation of cadres was rhetorically supported.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: Hoxhaism rejects bourgeois parliamentary forms and relies on vanguard-party leadership, so revocable delegation per policy area is not part of it.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine centres on class struggle and anti-imperialism, not global catastrophic risk, so this is not a priority.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Hoxhaism opposes religion altogether and so has no interest in religious offices; women's equality is supported generally but the question is moot.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Hoxha's regime promoted women's emancipation and legal equality in marriage, although Albanian patriarchal custom persisted.

missingStatements.text: Each country's revolution must be made by its own people and cannot be exported from abroad.
missingStatements.rationale: Hoxha states that revolution is carried out by the people of each country and is not exported, while still backing internationalist aid.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow intra-communist doctrine; socialism-one-country and dominated-front already separate the relevant camps.

missingStatements.text: The world's communist movement has been corrupted by revisionism, which restores capitalism from within.
missingStatements.rationale: Hoxha's core claim is that Khrushchev's, Tito's and Mao's leaders restored capitalism while keeping socialist words.

notes: The two proposals reflect positions not captured by the existing statements; Adherents might answer some moral-cultural items differently across later parties.
